what:
Validation-fixture authoring gotcha: `memories.softening.threshold` masks the hard-block path when seeding small memory sets.

**Default behavior:** `memories.softening.threshold: 10` — if a project has <10 total memories, pre-read-recall and pre-edit-recall downgrade ALL hard blocks to soft additionalContext nudges ("keeps small projects from feeling hostile").

**Impact on fixtures:** A validation fixture seeded with 8 memories (typical — a handful per layer) will never fire `decision: "block"` by default. Scenarios written around the hard-block render path will silently test the soft path instead. I hit this exactly once on 2026-04-22 while building the hook-visibility validation fixture — seeded 8 memories, expected hard block, saw soft inject.

**Fix:** write a `.aide/config.json` in the fixture dir overriding the threshold:
```json
{"memories": {"softening": {"threshold": 5}}}
```
Lower the threshold below the seeded count so forceSoft evaluates to false and the hard path fires. Applied to `/tmp/aide-hook-viz-validation/.aide/config.json`.

**Alternative fix:** seed enough memories (≥ threshold+1) to naturally clear the bar. More realistic but needs bulk seeding.

**Concrete reference:** `src/memory/hooks/handlers.ts` preRead/preEdit have:
```ts
const softeningThreshold = Number(getSetting(projectRoot, 'memories.softening.threshold') ?? 10);
const forceSoft = result.total_memories < softeningThreshold;
// ... if (forceSoft || encountered) soft else hard
```

Future validation fixtures should decide up-front: small realistic fixture (accept soft-only paths, adjust scenario expectations) or large/threshold-overridden fixture (all paths exercisable).
why: Hit this gotcha live while building /tmp/aide-hook-viz-validation. Took ~2 min to diagnose once the soft-path JSON came back from what I expected to be hard-block — obvious in hindsight but easy to miss when designing scenarios. Future session building a similar fixture will trip on the same thing without this note.
